apparatus.basis: Editor's restoration of the standard chapter-closing formula. ⲧⲉⲟⲩⲟ + 1sg perfect + 3pl suffix 'I have proclaimed them' + ⲁⲣⲱⲧⲛ̄ 'to you' + ⲛⲉⲓ̈ ⲛⲉ 'these are.' Followed by leer marking chapter end.

notes.decision: Preserved exactly as transcribed. Expected page numeral for page 103 would be ⲣⲅ̄. The transcribed ⲡⲣ̄ is anomalous — possibly a transcription artifact, scribal error, or unusual ligature. Retained as-is per fidelity to source.

Translated 'Itself it is the Darkness' rather than 'Likewise.' ⲍⲱⲱϩ here functions as the intensive/reflexive pronoun (= Sah. ϩⲱⲱϥ) in predicative position, identifying what 'the first Day' IS in correspondential terms — direct identification rather than comparison. The line continues the predicate-identification of the first Day from preceding page.

ⲙⲟⲩⲝⲧ̄ taken as Lyc. perfect/qualitative of ⲙⲟⲩϫⲧ̄ 'mingle' (ⲝ for ϫ). The Darkness 'was mingled with' the Five Sons — the standard Manichaean cosmogonic event in which the Five Light-Sons of First Man become entangled with primordial darkness.
Read as ⲛⲁ-ϩⲙⲟⲟⲥ-ⲧ̄ ⲁ-ⲛⲟⲩ-ⲑⲣⲟⲛⲟⲥ 'they shall sit upon their thrones,' the Lyc. ⲍ for ϩ and ⲫ for θ. Future III with directional ⲁ- = 'upon.' Apostrophe after ⲁⲍⲙⲉⲥⲧ marks word boundary.

Read ⲡⲥⲁ ⲙ̄ⲡⲧⲟⲩⲱⲍ 'the place/region of the dwelling' (Lyc. ⲍ for Sah. ⲥ orthographic alternation, or ⲥⲁ 'side, place'). The ⲡⲧⲟⲩⲱⲍ is verbal noun of ⲟⲩⲱⲍ 'dwell' (= Sah. ⲟⲩⲱϩ). The 'place of dwelling' is the abode established for the Light-Fathers in the new aeon.

Read as ⲛ̄-ⲧⲱⲱⲧ ⲙ̄-ⲡϣⲓ 'in the equal/proportion of the measure.' ⲧⲱⲧ 'be equal, agree' nominalized = 'equality, proportion.' The new aeon corresponds to the first Day in proportion of measure — the second Day matches the first by cosmic measure.
Taken as relative perfect 3pl with qualitative element of ⲱϩⲉ 'stand' = 'which stood/was-set.' Refers to the first Day as already established cosmic state.

Read as 'the great third of the Days' — ⲧⲧⲛⲁⲟ̄ either doubled article+ⲛⲁⲟ̄ 'the great' or substantival 'the great one.' ⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ = 'third' (Lyc. ⲙⲉϩ-ϣⲟⲙⲧ). Continues the enumeration: first Day, second Day, great third Day.
Lyc. qualitative of ϩⲗⲟϭ 'sweet' (cf. accumulated vocab ⲁⲡⲭⲗⲥⲉ/ⲡⲭⲗⲥⲉ 'sweetness'). The fragrance is gustatorily/olfactorily sweet — direct correspondential register.
Lyc. plural ⲛ̄-ⲓⲁⲧⲉ 'eyes' with 3pl possessive suffix -ⲟⲩ = 'their eyes' (cf. accumulated ⲛⲓⲁⲧⲉ 'eyes/Fathers'; here clearly eyes from context of seeing).

Tentatively read as ϩⲁ-ⲧⲁⲍⲙ-ⲟⲩ ⲁⲛ 'at their summoning, again.' From ⲧⲁⲍⲙ 'summon' (in accumulated vocab) with 3pl suffix. Alternative readings: 'with their blessing' (ϩⲁⲧⲁ-ⲥⲙⲟⲩ) or 'next to them' all uncertain.

Tentatively read as Lyc. reflexive 'they themselves' (parallel to Sah. ⲙⲁⲩⲁⲁⲩ 'themselves alone'). The construction places it adverbially with 'shall be perfected' = 'they themselves shall be perfected.'
Possessive ⲡⲉⲥ-/ⲧⲉⲥ- = 'her' (3sg.f), referring to a feminine antecedent — likely the εἰκὼν 'image' (line 6, 11, fem.) or perhaps each soul individually. Translated 'her aeon, her tabernacle.'

Tentatively read ⲁϥ-ⲡⲱϩ ⲛ̄-ⲟⲩⲱⲗⲡ 'he attains/reaches to reveal' — ⲡⲱϩ 'reach' + infinitive ⲛ̄-. Alternative: ⲁϩⲡⲍ̄ as a hapax verb. The sense is that the Father, after promising not to hide, reaches forth in continual revelation.

Read as 'the two Deaths likewise that I have [proclaimed].' ⲡⲙⲟⲩ ⲥⲛⲉⲩ = 'two Deaths' (parallel to the three great Days as cosmic-eschatological dyad). ⲉⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲧⲉ = relative perfect 1sg with 3pl object 'that I have...them' completed by editor restoration. The chapter closes by recapitulating the three Days and two Deaths.
